messages.content: I have a New Orleans installation coming up. I need to fly from Atlanta on Sunday, January 11, because I have to be at the museum by 8:00 Monday morning. The installation should finish around 4:00 Wednesday, but they may add an inspection Thursday morning. Can we sort out flights and what hotel dates make sense without locking the wrong return?

Yes. What museum are you reporting to, and how late would you be comfortable arriving Sunday? I can compare the outbound choices first, then lay out Wednesday evening and Thursday returns alongside a hotel plan that keeps the contingency manageable.
The Contemporary Arts Center at 900 Camp Street. I would rather not arrive so late that Sunday becomes exhausting, but I do not need to spend the whole day there either.

For Sunday, January 11, the most practical nonstop choices from ATL to MSY are: Delta at 2:10 p.m., arriving 2:48 p.m. local time for $189 one way; Southwest at 3:45 p.m., arriving 4:25 p.m. for $174; and Delta at 5:35 p.m., arriving 6:10 p.m. for $162. Each is about 1 hour 40 minutes in the air. The 3:45 Southwest flight gives you a useful middle ground: enough time at home Sunday morning, arrival before dinner, and plenty of margin before the 8:00 a.m. report time.
How much risk is there with the 5:35 Delta? I could still be at a hotel by 7:30 or so if it is on time.

That timing is reasonable. A 6:10 p.m. arrival would typically put you near Camp Street around 7:00 to 7:25 by taxi or rideshare, depending on baggage and traffic. Even a delay of an hour would still leave a workable evening. The tradeoff is simply less recovery time if the flight slips substantially; it does not put Monday's start in jeopardy unless there is a major disruption.
Then keep the 5:35 Delta as the leading outbound. What can I do Wednesday after a 4:00 p.m. finish? I will have a checked case with work materials, so assume I need a real airport buffer.

The first return I would consider is Delta leaving MSY at 7:20 p.m. Wednesday and arriving ATL at 9:48 p.m. At a 4:00 p.m. finish, leaving the museum by 4:20 should get you to the airport around 4:50 to 5:15, leaving roughly two hours before departure for the checked case. There is also a Southwest nonstop at 8:35 p.m., arriving Atlanta at 11:05 p.m. It provides more margin but makes for a later night. I would not recommend the 5:40 p.m. Delta because your workday and checked materials make that connection to the airport too tight.
Agreed, 5:40 is out. What are the fares for 7:20 and 8:35, and can either one be changed after Monday without losing the ticket value?

The Wednesday 7:20 Delta is currently $214 one way in Main Cabin. It has no change fee, but you would pay any fare difference; canceling before departure leaves an eCredit rather than a cash refund. The 8:35 Southwest option is $196 in Wanna Get Away Plus, also with no change fee, and the value can be retained as a transferable flight credit under that fare. Neither is a refundable cash fare at those prices.
Since I may not know about Thursday until sometime Monday, show me Thursday options too. The inspection, if it happens, should be over by 10:30 a.m.

On Thursday, January 15, Delta has nonstops at 1:20 p.m., arriving ATL at 3:47 p.m., and 3:55 p.m., arriving at 6:23 p.m. The current Main Cabin fares are $178 and $166. Southwest has a 2:30 p.m. nonstop arriving at 4:58 p.m. for $171. The 1:20 Delta is possible if the inspection ends at 10:30 and you leave promptly, but the 2:30 Southwest or 3:55 Delta gives you more room for an overrun and handling the work case.
The 1:20 sounds unnecessarily tight. Keep the 3:55 Delta as the Thursday fallback so both likely flights are with Delta. Can Delta combine the Sunday outbound with an undecided return somehow?

You can book the Sunday flight as a one-way ticket and add the return later. Delta does not offer a multi-day hold that would preserve both Wednesday and Thursday fares while you wait. Another option is to book one return now and change it Monday, but the new fare could be higher or lower, and the original ticket would not protect space on the other flight. Separate one-way tickets are the cleanest arrangement while the return date is unresolved.
Do not book the return yet. Is there a reason not to book the Sunday flight now?

No operational reason. The Sunday 5:35 p.m. Delta nonstop is fixed regardless of the inspection decision, and its current $162 Main Cabin fare can be changed or canceled for an eCredit before departure. Booking it now isolates the settled part of the trip. I would only wait if your employer requires the outbound and return to be ticketed together.

They allow separate tickets. Hold off on actually purchasing anything today, though. I need the comparison for approval. Let's look at hotels near the Contemporary Arts Center. I will be alone, one room.

For January 11 onward, three nearby options stand out. The Higgins Hotel is about a 12-minute walk and is $219 per night before tax. Cambria Hotel New Orleans Downtown is about a 9-minute walk at $187. The Virgin Hotels New Orleans is about a 10-minute walk at $205. All three have rooms available through Thursday morning, January 15; estimated totals for four nights are $1,013 at the Higgins, $867 at Cambria, and $948 at Virgin, including taxes.
Cambria is enough for this trip. But I do not want to pay Wednesday night if the inspection is canceled and I fly home that evening. Can the last night be separated?

Yes. Cambria can be arranged as one refundable reservation for Sunday through Wednesday morning, January 11-14, plus a separate refundable reservation for Wednesday night, checking out Thursday, January 15. The first three nights total about $651 including taxes. The separate Wednesday night is about $216 including taxes and can be canceled without penalty until 6:00 p.m. local time Tuesday, January 13. The hotel can link the reservations so you should be able to remain in the same room if the inspection is added, although the front desk may need to refresh your key.

That is the structure I need. If the Thursday inspection is confirmed Monday, I keep both hotel pieces and take the 3:55 Delta Thursday. If it is canceled, I cancel the separate Wednesday night by Tuesday evening and aim for the 7:20 Delta Wednesday. Is the Wednesday flight still realistic if installation slips to 4:30?

It remains possible, but the margin becomes narrower. Departing the museum around 4:45 would likely put you at MSY between 5:15 and 5:40, leaving about 1 hour 40 minutes before the 7:20 flight. That normally clears Delta's checked-bag cutoff, but a longer overrun or heavy traffic could create trouble. The 8:35 Southwest would be the safer same-day backup if the finish time starts moving later.
Put the 8:35 Southwest in the notes as the backup, not the main choice. Also, confirm exactly which dates I should request approval for, including the possible extra hotel night.

Request approval for travel from Sunday, January 11 through either Wednesday, January 14 or Thursday, January 15. The working itinerary is the Delta nonstop from ATL at 5:35 p.m. Sunday, arriving MSY at 6:10 p.m.; a probable Delta return at 7:20 p.m. Wednesday, arriving ATL at 9:48 p.m.; and, if the inspection is added, the Delta return at 3:55 p.m. Thursday, arriving at 6:23 p.m. Cambria would be requested as a three-night stay from January 11-14, estimated at $651 including taxes, with a separately cancelable January 14-15 night estimated at $216. The Wednesday 8:35 p.m. Southwest nonstop is noted only as a backup if installation runs past 4:00. Nothing has been booked.
